correctness.rationale: In a simple graph the vertices W incident to no selected edge are independent, and every edge inside the complementary red set must be selected (otherwise two distinct selected edges dominate it). A red vertex must have a red neighbor, and if it has a white neighbor it must have precisely one red neighbor. These rules are sufficient and recover W uniquely from the selected set. On degree-two paths they reduce to white spacing at least three, with a red penultimate vertex next to a leaf. With a red hub either all neighbors are red or exactly one is red; the latter neighbor is on the cycle (two orientations) or in one designated arm. With a white hub, both vertices next to each end of the cycle path and each of the first two arm vertices are red, which rules out length-one arms. The cycle word counts are I_(c-3), I_(c-5), and I_(c-7) for the three red-hub endpoint types, with both-white impossible at c=3,4 and one remaining permitted endpoint pattern at c=5. Both-end two-zero forcing gives I_(c-5) for the white hub, including overlapping prefixes at c=3,4. Splitting arm words by their last bit, a final 1 forces its immediately preceding two positions (where present) to zero, including the already-red penultimate. This gives the displayed I formulas, base triples and recurrence. Thus cases are disjoint and exhaustive, and the length-one and length-two formulas follow by substitution for r>=2. Independently enumerated all edge subsets for 93 small heterogeneous or boundary instances, with c=3..7, r=2 or 3, lengths 1..4 and total order at most 12, directly imposing the outside-edge test; all agreed. Examples: c=3 gives 3 and 5 for arms (1,1) and (2,2), and c=5 with arms (1,2) gives 8. The symbolic proof, not the finite check, establishes the unrestricted result.

evidence: Theorem 4.4 gives a linear-time counting algorithm for generalized series-parallel graphs, which include the audited graphs. The P6-free paper describes restricted algorithms, and Theorem 5.2 of the counting paper gives the cycle recurrence.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A parse-tree algorithm can calculate individual counts but is not itself the explicit joint length formula, root-class decomposition or subdivision asymptotics. The cycle and P6-free restrictions do not state the unrestricted arm-length result.

evidence: The lollipop theorem also has a strict cycle bound at fixed order; the general paper conjectures the corresponding bound for connected graphs. The bouquet result accounts for hub spokes, but each petal meets the hub in two neighbors and has no leaf boundary.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither a one-arm extremal comparison nor the cycle recurrence entails a linear-versus-exponential arm-number contrast. The four cases and leaf boundary give an additional exact derivation; the frozen result does not claim the general cycle bound.

evidence: 381ff49f7243 gives the exact bivariate rational enumerator for one tail. 2e80dff19ef1 has a hub-refined product for cycle petals, with no pendant leaves.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The red/white degree rule is shared; neither replacing a cycle petal by a path nor multiplying one-tail counts preserves the hub constraints. The new factorization distinguishes a single red neighbor on the cycle from one on an arm, and the length-one obstruction at a white hub is specific to leaves.

originality.rationale: The new content supported by the inspected sources is the four-class product for one cycle with at least two independently sized pendant paths, and the resulting change of growth under single subdivision of all arms. The one-tail count, hub-refined cycle-bouquet product, and generalized series-parallel counting algorithm are genuine overlaps in method or scope, but none supplies this multiarm statement.
residual_risks: A prior explicit transfer-state specialization on one-hub graphs could subsume the formula; the inspected algorithms were not claimed to exclude every such derivation.

value.rationale: The formula classifies every feasible edge set with arbitrary heterogeneous arm lengths, including when a length-one arm blocks an entire root class. It also proves an at-most-affine versus exponential dependence on the number of arms for every fixed cycle size. This is a structural benchmark beyond evaluation of a single graph and does not imply the general extremal conjecture.
